# Background Information!

## As of 2026, California has: {style="color: deeppink"}

-   \$16.90 statewide minimum wage

    -   Adjusted for inflation based on the ***national*** consumer price index for urban wage earners and clerical workers (CPI-W)

        -   Federal levels of inflation are often lower than the state's...

-   40 cities/counties with higher wage ordinances

-   \$20 minimum wage for fast food workers (AB1228)

-   And more...

## Wage Distribution

```{r}
# load in packages
library(tidyverse)
library(readr)
library(readxl)

## Index of ALL California Cities/Counties with wage variance

# read in CSV file
cali_wages <- read_csv("CaliforniaCityMinimumWages.csv")
ggplot(cali_wages, aes(x = Rate, y = Locality, fill = grepl("Emeryville|West Hollywood", Locality))) +
  geom_col() +
  geom_text(aes(label = paste("$", format(round(Rate, 2)))),
            hjust = -0.1,
            size = 2.5) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "red", "FALSE" = "grey60"), guide = "none") +
  labs(
    y = "California Cities",
    x = "Minimum Wage Rates ($)",
    title = "All California Cities with Wage Variance (2026)"
  ) +
  theme(
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 6)
  )
```

# A Problem {style="color: deeppink"}

Initiatives to continue raising the minimum wage annually exemplify that our statewide minimum wage is NOT high enough, but allowing cities to set their own wages can prove to be costly in other ways for Californians...

-   Commuting for higher pay in minimum wage jobs

    -   What's stopping somebody in Anaheim (\$16.90) from driving to LA (\$18.42) for a higher pay in the same job?

    -   SoCal is home to the WORST commutes in America!

# One Proposition {style="color: deeppink"}

Set a baseline statewide minimum wage and increase annually based on CPI-W increases in California's Metropolitan Statistical Areas (MSAs) to ensure more accurate wage indexes.

# Simulation Example

```{r}
# read in excel file 
LA_MSA <- read_excel("LA_MSA.xlsx")
# remove unnecessary rows
newLA_df <- LA_MSA[-c(1:10), ] # now df displays CPI-W by month and year 

# make year column as.numeric
newLA_df[[1]] <- as.numeric(newLA_df[[1]], na.rm = TRUE)

# create a function to calculate rates of changes for the past 5 years
avg_function <- function(year) {
  year_col <- newLA_df[[1]]
  prev <- newLA_df[year_col == year - 1, 8:13]
  now <- newLA_df[year_col == year, 2:7]
  mean(as.numeric(c(unlist(prev), unlist(now))), na.rm = TRUE)
}
years <- 2022:2026 # the past 5 years

# create a data frame using the rates from above
rates <- data.frame(
  year = years,
  new_avg = sapply(years, avg_function),
  old_avg = sapply(years - 1, avg_function)
)
rates$x <- rates$new_avg / rates$old_avg # calculate rates of change

# calculate hypothetical minimum wages for the LA MSA area from 2022-2026
year_one <- rates$x[1] * 14.00 # $14.00 was California's statewide minimum wage in 2021
year_two <- rates$x[2] * year_one # 2023
year_three <- rates$x[3] * year_two # 2024
year_four <- rates$x[4] * year_three # 2025
year_five <- rates$x[5] * year_four # 2026

## create data frames for the hypothetical, California actual, and LA actual
hypo_wagedf <- data.frame(
  year = rates$year,
  wage = c(year_one, year_two, year_three, year_four, year_five)
) # hypothetical

cali_wagedf <- data.frame(
  year = rates$year,
  wage = c("15.00", "15.50", "16.00", "16.50", "16.90")
) # california

LA_wagedf <- data.frame(
  year = rates$year,
  wage = c("16.04", "16.78", "17.28", "17.87", "18.42")
) # LA

# rename to create separate columns
hypo_wagedf$series <- "Hypothetical"
cali_wagedf$series <- "California"
LA_wagedf$series <- "Los Angeles"

# collapse into one data frame
all_wages <- rbind(hypo_wagedf, cali_wagedf, LA_wagedf)
all_wages$wage <- as.numeric(all_wages$wage) # convert wages from strings into numbers

# line plot for all wages!
ggplot(all_wages, aes(x = year, y = wage, color = series)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    x = "Year",
    y = "Minimum Wage ($)",
  )

```

# Data Challenges {style="color: deeppink"}

The Federal Government only provides MSA inflation data for a select few MSA locations in California:

-   Los Angeles-Long Beach-Anaheim

-   Riverside-San Bernardino-Ontario

-   San Diego-Carlsbad

-   San Francisco-Oakland-Hayward

And some inflation data only records every other month...

# Project Challenges {style="color: deeppink"}

-   What to do when projected wages are significantly less than the wages already put in place?
